summary: A 1934 hip-roof L-4 cab in the Lolo National Forest, the last of its kind in western Montana, now rented overnight through recreation.gov.

facts.design: L-4 ground house cab with a hip roof, built pre-1936
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Missoula Ranger District, Lolo National Forest)

access.note: Rented overnight via recreation.gov; Forest Road 37 closed Dec 1-May 1.

visit.trail_note: Road closed Dec 1-May 1; reach by hiking, skiing or snowmobiling about 7.5 miles in winter.

events.note: Extensively renovated by the Montana Chapter of the Forest Fire Lookout Association after its active fire-watch service ended; exact year not given
Registered June 5, 1996 as US 173, MT 15, nominated by Gary Weber of the FFLA

evidence.quote: This L-4 cab, built in 1934, is available on the Recreation Rental program.

evidence.supports: 20 miles southwest of Missoula, Lolo National Forest
evidence.quote:
Lolo National Forest
20 miles southwest of Missoula

evidence.supports: only pre-1936 hip-roof L-4 ground house remaining in western Montana
evidence.quote: West Fork Butte is the only pre-1936 design hip-roof L-4 ground house lookout remaining in western Montana.

evidence.supports: staffed into the late 1980s; renovated by Montana FFLA chapter
evidence.quote: It was generally staffed up to the late 1980s and has been extensively renovated by the Montana Chapter of the Forest Fire Lookout Association.

evidence.supports: sleeps four, bunk beds, propane stove, wood stove, vault toilet
evidence.quote: The lookout can sleep up to four people and is equipped with bunk beds and mattress pads. The lookout also has a table and chairs, a propane cook stove and lantern, as well as a wood stove for heat.

evidence.supports: road closed Dec 1-May 1, reach by hiking/skiing/snowmobiling ~7.5 miles
evidence.quote: From December 1 - May 1 Forest Road 37 is closed, requiring hiking, skiing or snowmobiling roughly 7.5 miles to the facility.

evidence.supports: road can be muddy, snowy or icy outside those dates; guests on their own
evidence.quote: Outside of these dates the road may be muddy, snowy or icy - guests are responsible for their own travel arrangements and safety and must bring several of their own amenities.

notes_for_editor: Thin on named staffing history and exact renovation date; NHLR gives only 'late 1980s' for last staffing and no year for the FFLA restoration. Elevation differs slightly between sources (firelookout.com: 6,157 ft; nhlr: 6,102 ft/1,860 m, matching the tower record), not flagged as a correction since it's a minor rounding-level discrepancy already reflected in the record. Did not use the full 2-search/8-read budget; cached local pages (firelookout.com, nhlr.org) plus the record's own recreation.gov text were sufficient for an honest, modest-length story.
